keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1150-1449: the page says the polity 'was established in the northwestern basin of Lake Titicaca and covered 20.000 square kilometres', capital Hatunqulla 34 km north of Puno, Azángaro the capital of Umasuyu; no exact boundaries (Ayaviri is a battle site). The Aymara kingdoms page extends the Colla territory at its conquest 'from the Pacific coast across the Qullaw plateau to the Mojeños mountains'. A disc of 80 km round Juliaca less Puno's 30 km (about 17,000 km2) stands for it. [Reviewer am-04, 2026-10-19: the Colla extent now also subtracts the 45 km Ilave disc of lupaca-kingdom, which overlapped it by 4 cells (about 1,000 km2)]

ledger.note: 1445-1450: Pachacuti defeats the Colla at Ayaviri. The war was 'between 1445 and 1450'; the Colla chief waited for the Inca at Ayaviri; Pachacuti then went to Hatuncolla, organised Inca administration and ordered forts built; the chief, Chuchic Capac, was captured and the Colla Kingdom ended, 'Incan victory'. The Colla page's infobox gives the conquest c. 1463 and a revolt crushed by Topa Inca Yupanqui c. 1483; the Lupaca page has the Lupaca-Colla revolt c. 1473.

wars.outcome: Inca victory under Pachacuti (his general Apo Conde Mayta at the border in one version): battle at Ayaviri, Colla chief captured, the Colla and the Lupaca on the northwest shore of Lake Titicaca conquered; Rowe puts the southern border at the Desaguadero, Pärssinen beyond it toward Lake Poopó.
wars.note: The List of wars page dates the Colla-Inca War 1445-1550 (the revolts) and a 13th-century Battle of Huaychu between the Kingdom of Cusco and the Colla (Inca victory); the Colla page's infobox says c. 1463.

wars.name: Colla-Lupaca rivalry
wars.outcome: A rivalry placed in the 14th century; under Viracocha Inca the Colla ruler (Cari on the Aymara kingdoms page) invaded Lupaca territory and was defeated at Paucarcolla. No border moved.
wars.note: No year on the pages; the range is Viracocha Inca's reign (c. 1380-1438 across the two chronologies).

certainty.note: No boundaries on either page; Ayaviri is a battle site.

notes: Wikipedia's article is 'Colla Kingdom'. End 1450 from the Colla-Inca war page ('between 1445 and 1450', 'the Colla Kingdom ended'); the Colla page's own infobox says the Inca conquest c. 1463 and the revolt crushed c. 1483, and the Lupaca page gives the Lupaca-Colla revolt c. 1473: three dates for the end of independence. Cliopatria's Inca 1450 shape holds the north-west Titicaca shore (about 4,000 km2 within 50 km of Puno), which supports the war page's date over 1463. Hatunqulla is not a gazetteer place (gazetteer_names_needed). The List of wars page also mentions a Battle of Huaychu (13th century) between the Kingdom of Cusco and the Colla (Inca victory), not drawn.
